reporting.continuity: Extend Abacus 2.0 report/document layouts, spreadsheet fields and one-off/repeating sections.
reporting.presentation: Retain standard TUI editing/navigation; add capability-aware graphical preview with titles, axes and legends. Support monochrome patterns and available display modes through the display API.
reporting.output: Print reports and charts through supported printer drivers; define pagination and refresh stale query/formula results before output.

data_interchange.bpi_continuity: Retain versioned BPI summary imports as independent planning inputs with reconciliation and decimal validation; no ledger write-back or live database connection.
data_interchange.csv: Schema-mapped CSV import with quoted fields, delimiter/character encoding selection, explicit date and decimal conventions, null handling, text preservation for identifiers and rejected-record diagnostics. Provide value-only CSV export with explicit loss-of-formulas/types warning.
data_interchange.vsam: Import host-exported sequential logical records from supported VSAM datasets using a supplied field/record layout. Host-side export (for example IDCAMS REPRO) and a documented transfer path are prerequisites; raw VSAM clusters, indexes and disk images are not desktop interchange formats.
data_interchange.vsam_conversion: Declare supported record boundaries, lengths, offsets, keys and character encoding; convert EBCDIC, supported binary, packed-decimal and zoned-decimal fields explicitly. Reject unsupported layouts without silently changing values.
data_interchange.migration: Versioned document format; preserve supported older worksheets and reports. Older Abacus/Pulse editions must reject unsupported new features before writing. Explicit value-only export is a lossy interchange option.

release_scope.launch: Flat typed formatted tables, bounded columnar processing, virtual columns, unique-key lookups, a documented read-only SQL subset, graphical reports, embedded Pulse and mapped imports.

Broader query capabilities and competitive response to Lotus 1-2-3 in a later Abacus version.
release_scope.resource_policy: Qualify real Artemis 128/256 KiB configurations and later Artemis PRO separately. Record application/OS memory, storage, dataset size and timings; larger jobs may require expansion or disk-backed execution. No new minimum RAM or maximum row count is asserted.
release_scope.acceptance_workflow: Import sales records, join customer/product information, calculate margins, group by region, print a graphical report, save/reopen, then repeat using a Pulse script.
acceptance_requirements: Measure memory, disk I/O, import/query/recalculation/report times and compression on named datasets.
Verify import conversion/rejections, decimal rounding, nulls, duplicate lookup keys and join cardinality.
Verify cancellation, grouped undo, edit visibility, dependency invalidation, save recovery and unsupported-version rejection.

requirements: Checked user pointers and protected kernel/device mappings

Per-process memory, file and request limits

implementation_design.title: BPI transactional client/server v1
implementation_design.architecture: Thin Z80/ERA clients send bounded business operations to an Artemis PRO server. Query evaluation, indexes, validation, accounting posting and transactions execute on the server; clients do not fetch arbitrary database pages.

transactions.concurrency: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.
transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

protocol.transport: Length-framed requests over TCP; bounded messages and chunked results.
protocol.duplicate_suppression: Store committed write request IDs and outcomes durably. After reconnect, clients query status or retry with the same ID; never post the same payment twice.

implementation_design.title: BPI transactional client/server v1
implementation_design.architecture: Thin Z80/ERA clients send bounded business operations to an Artemis PRO server. Query evaluation, indexes, validation, accounting posting and transactions execute on the server; clients do not fetch arbitrary database pages.

transactions.concurrency: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.
transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

subcomponents.name: Disk browser
subcomponents.description: Own disk/file browsing workflows, using system list controls, dialogs and file services.

subcomponents.name: Calculator

subcomponents.name: Calendar / scheduler

runtime_notes: The cartridge remains a 16 KB product capacity; removing duplicate routines does not establish a measured free-space budget.

Code executes from banked ROM where practical; writable application state is held in RAM.

Application-specific text editing, file browsing, calculation and scheduling logic remain in this cartridge.

A resident workspace reserves RAM explicitly; the cartridge does not imply multitasking.

software_edition.name: Aurelia Software Compatibility Kit (CP/M edition)
software_edition.description: Manufacturer and independent-integrator kit for implementing the released Aurelia application environment on independently designed computers.

contents: Published processor, CP/M, memory, display, keyboard, storage and error-behaviour contracts
Reference runtime adapter source and redistribution terms
Diagnostics and conformance tests, including resource limits and failure cases
Abacus and Business Tools acceptance workloads: calculations, file interchange, printing, save/reopen
Porting and troubleshooting manuals, source listings and machine-readable disks
Versioned results forms and optional certification submission requirements

compatibility_policy.eligibility: Any manufacturer or independent integrator may implement the published environment without a bespoke partnership or mandatory certification.
compatibility_policy.binary: Existing Z80 binaries require compatible instruction execution and the specified OS/runtime and memory behaviour; CP/M alone is insufficient. Other processors need an appropriate port or execution solution.
compatibility_policy.hardware: Native video, keyboards, disks and printers may be exposed through adapters. FlexiBUS and Logix video hardware are separate optional profiles. Full hardware clones may implement those published interfaces under their applicable terms.
compatibility_policy.applications: Named supported platforms are tested configurations, not an exclusive permission list. Independently implemented environments may run properly licensed applications; certification identifies precisely what AION tested.
compatibility_policy.delivery: Printed manuals/source listings and disks; host/media conversion quoted separately.
compatibility_policy.certification: Optional, configuration- and version-specific. Manufacturer-declared compatibility is distinct from AION-tested application compatibility. FlexiBUS electrical/protocol and Logix display tests are separate claims.
